stats.torah_summary: Torah #130 opens with the Talmudic maxim 'kol ha-gadol me-chavero, yitzro gadol mimenu' (the greater a person is, the greater his evil inclination — Sukkah 52). The Rebbe's teaching is a single, tight eitza argument: humility (ענוה) → sexual purity / shmirat ha-brit (שמירת הברית). The proof moves through: (1) the Talmudic teaching that arrogance leads to adultery (Sotah 4b); (2) the biblical juxtaposition of 'Moshe was very humble' with 'Miriam and Aaron spoke about Moshe' regarding his Kushite wife — the Torah answers that Moshe's total humility enabled complete abstinence (perישut); (3) the Talmudic teaching that 'Yosef's strength was Boaz's humility / Boaz's strength was Palti ben Laish's humility' (Sanhedrin 19b); (4) the re-reading of the opening maxim: 'gadol' = one who has gaavah (pride), 'yitzro gadol' = the yetzer hara overpowers him in sexual lust — because as the Zohar states (Vayikra 15b): 'the essence of the evil inclination is to expose nakedness/illicit relations'. The Torah's entire structure is eitza (causal): gadlut/gaavah → yetzer dominates through niuf; its inverse (ענוה) → saved from niuf / shmirat ha-brit.
